title: [Design attempt 6 amendment, A-5] Baseline: pin current FLISR behaviour and record failing reproductions on the unmodified base backend/ tree @ 20d2a30 (PR #13)
safety: safety-critical (inherited, STD-REQ-6). Test-only, but lands in the change set that touches protected backend/app/flisr.py: two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
scope_notes: [Design attempt 5 amendment, A-4.2] Safety skill steps 1-3 (STD-SAFETY-2, STD-SAFETY-3). No production file may change in this unit; every test is written and run against the base backend/ tree of agent/rca-backfeed/fix @ 20d2a303c9548f9f7170cb3dfef1487fb7e9a009 (DEF-FLISR-7 PR #13, Q-DESIGN-3). Before starting, check `git diff 20d2a30 <branch point> -- backend/` is empty; otherwise stop (base drift) and return the run to Design.

Characterization (REQ-TIECAP-22): @pytest.mark.characterization tests through the legacy tie_capacity_kw interface, restricted to inputs where every candidate tie has a finite, non-negative entry with L <= C or L > C + 0.5 kW. They pin isolation steps, restoration steps and their order, customers_restored, customers_remaining, transferred_load_kw. They do not pin notes text (REQ-TIECAP-12 changes it) and exclude C in (L, L + 0.5], missing entries, NaN/+-inf/negative (intended changes 1-3 of the specification).

Characterization inputs exclude faults on a section with a SCADA tie at either endpoint (DEF-FLISR-7 is handled incorrectly today; pinning it would mask or block that separate defect run, spec section 3).

REQ-TIECAP-19: pin the no-fault plan field-by-field (no isolation, no restoration, manual-patrol note, customers_remaining) and assert plan.model_dump().get('blocked_ties', []) == [] so the same test passes unchanged on main and after U2/U3.

Reproductions (STD-SAFETY-3), kept failing output for the PR: (a) shipped model, CB-1201 open, no capacity entry: plan carries no machine-readable reason for skipping TIE-1201-1405 (expects blocked_ties CAPACITY_UNKNOWN); (b) legacy tie_capacity_kw NaN and +inf: plan closes TIE-1201-1405 (expects no close step). Committed as pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason='REPRO ...') so main stays green; U3 removes only the markers.
backend/tests/test_flisr.py is not in any unit: it must pass unchanged to the end of the run.
[Design attempt 5 amendment, A-4.2] Characterization also excludes ties held by the DEF-FLISR-7 guard (pinned by the base's own tests) and invalid section loads (Q-DESIGN-2).
oracle: [Design attempt 6 amendment, A-5] Characterization: the values measured on the unmodified base backend/ tree of agent/rca-backfeed/fix @ 20d2a303c9548f9f7170cb3dfef1487fb7e9a009 (PR #13) are the oracle (re-run must be identical before and after U2-U4). title: Domain types: TieCapacity, BlockedTie and RestorationPlan.blocked_ties
safety: safety-critical (inherited, STD-REQ-6). models.py is not a protected path, but the types gate which ties FLISR closes and ship in the protected-path change set: two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
scope_notes: [Design attempt 5 amendment, A-4.2] Additive only: TieCapacity{kw, timestamp, quality} with extra fields forbidden; BlockedTie{tie_id, reason}; reason enum with 5 members in precedence order {FAULTED_SECTION, CAPACITY_INVALID, CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, CAPACITY_STALE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED} (REQ-TIECAP-11 amended per Q-DESIGN-3); RestorationPlan.blocked_ties default [].

Strictness per field, not model-wide ConfigDict(strict=True): measured on pydantic 2.14.1 / fastapi 0.143.1, model-wide strict makes FastAPI reject valid ISO-8601 datetime strings (spec section 4 design note). kw strict JSON number (string/bool/null rejected), NaN/+-inf/negative accepted; timestamp ISO-8601 string only, timezone-aware, JSON number and naive rejected; quality strict str; no clock comparison in the model.
No change to build_plan or api.py in this unit; U1 characterization must stay green.
oracle: Model unit tests per accept/reject class listed in REQ-TIECAP-1 ('yesterday', 1790000000, naive '2026-10-15T22:00:00', '2000', true, extra field -> reject; NaN, -1.0, +02:00 offset -> accept) validated both via model_validate_json and via a FastAPI TestClient echo route defined inside the test, so the HTTP (Python-mode) validation path is exercised; inspection of models.py; U1 suite re-run green.

title: Planner and endpoint: build_plan tie-capacity evaluation, legacy compatibility and POST /flisr/plan validation
safety: safety-critical (inherited, STD-REQ-6). Touches protected path backend/app/flisr.py: two human reviewers required irrespective of agent confidence (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
scope_notes: Why one unit for two modules: REQ-TIECAP-15 and REQ-TIECAP-16 each state a build_plan clause and an HTTP clause, and the legacy tie_capacity_kw path (REQ-TIECAP-16) must be migrated in the same step as the new tie_capacity path or the U1 characterization (which uses the legacy interface) breaks or REQ-TIECAP-5's inspection of flisr.py:98 fails in an intermediate state. Splitting would require a transiently non-conforming unit.

[SUPERSEDED by Design attempt 6 amendment, A-5; see the next note] Smallest fail-safe change (STD-SAFETY-4): remove the 0.0 default at flisr.py:98; per-tie usability with precedence INVALID > UNKNOWN > STALE > EXCEEDED; close iff L <= C + 0.5 kW; as_of read once per call (REQ-TIECAP-20); blocked ties add only to customers_remaining (REQ-TIECAP-18); one note per blocked tie (REQ-TIECAP-12).

[Design attempt 6 amendment, A-5] Replaces the preceding note. Smallest fail-safe change (STD-SAFETY-4): remove the 0.0 default at flisr.py:98; tie-loop order per design.md section 4: empty-candidate skip -> section-load check for every candidate tie, held or not (Q-DESIGN-2, FlisrError, no plan) -> DEF-FLISR-7 guard unchanged (FAULTED_SECTION) -> L precondition -> tie_capacity_verdict; per-tie precedence FAULTED_SECTION > CAPACITY_INVALID > CAPACITY_UNKNOWN > CAPACITY_STALE > CAPACITY_EXCEEDED (REQ-TIECAP-9 amended); close iff L <= C + 0.5 kW; as_of read once per call (REQ-TIECAP-20); blocked ties add only to customers_remaining, per amended REQ-TIECAP-18 (capacity-blocked: all candidate sections; FAULTED_SECTION: candidate sections other than the faulted one); one note per blocked tie (REQ-TIECAP-12; FAULTED_SECTION keeps the PR #13 note).

models.py is in scope only for response fields the Design stage places on RestorationPlan (as_of, deprecations, REQ-TIECAP-14/16) and for request types; the TieCapacity/BlockedTie definitions from U2 are not to be changed.

api.py: injectable server clock (spec section 4) for REQ-TIECAP-23 boundary tests; 422 before the planner runs for every malformed body (each 422 test asserts build_plan was not called); 200 with blocked_ties, never 409, for a blocked tie; OpenAPI description carries the deprecation and mutual-exclusion note (REQ-TIECAP-17).
Remove only the xfail markers in test_flisr_tie_capacity_repro.py; the repro tests must then pass unmodified otherwise.

Out of scope (spec section 3): DEF-FLISR-7 / _isolation_switches, locate_fault, SCADA adapter, shared alternate-feeder capacity, partial pick-up, console/**, state_estimator.py, agc.py, savecase.py, firmware/**, legacy/**.

[Design attempt 5 amendment, A-4.2] The two base DEF-FLISR-7 test files may be edited only under design.md section 6.1 (exclude as_of/blocked_ties/deprecations from model_dump or pass a fixed as_of; add blocked_ties assertions; replace the old skip-note text only); no expected switching step, order, count or transferred_load_kw may change. PR #14's test_flisr_def_flisr_7_qa.py is out of scope.

[Design attempt 5 amendment, A-4.2] Tie loop order: empty-candidate skip -> section-load precondition for every candidate tie, held or not (Q-DESIGN-2, FlisrError) -> DEF-FLISR-7 guard unchanged (FAULTED_SECTION) -> L precondition -> tie_capacity_verdict. Accounting per amended REQ-TIECAP-18.
oracle: Independent closed-form checks in the QA tests, not importing app.network or app.flisr helpers: QA-owned BFS over the test topology for the candidate node set and L (spec definitions), L <= C + 0.5 kW, age > 20 s, age < -2 s, quality == 'GOOD', math.isfinite(kw) and kw >= 0, the REQ-TIECAP-9 precedence function, and the as_of bound [server_now - 60 s, server_now + 2 s]. title: Safety invariant: no tie closed without usable capacity and L <= C + 0.5 kW, over >= 500 seeded cases
safety: safety-critical (inherited, STD-REQ-6). Test-only; ships in the protected-path change set: two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
scope_notes: STD-SAFETY-5: at least 500 seeded random cases over radial and branched feeders with one or more SCADA ties; capacity maps covering missing, non-GOOD, stale, boundary age, future-dated, NaN/+-inf, negative, below/at/above L + 0.5 kW; injected as_of.

The seeded generator in backend/tests/rca_def_flisr_7_sweep.py (branch agent/rca-backfeed/explore, not on main) may be copied into this one file; it only places ties at the feeder tail, so the generator must also place ties elsewhere to exercise multi-tie per-tie blocking.

[SUPERSEDED by Design attempt 6 amendment, A-5; see the next note] The invariant is about capacity gating only; it must neither assert nor exclude DEF-FLISR-7 back-feed (spec section 3). The oracle reproduces the specification's candidate-set definition, including today's pick-up semantics.

[Design attempt 6 amendment, A-5] Replaces the preceding note. The invariant covers capacity gating and the DEF-FLISR-7 hold as amended by Q-DESIGN-3 (REQ-TIECAP-21 amended): it asserts that a tie whose pick-up set contains an endpoint of the faulted section is FAULTED_SECTION and never closed, and that an invalid candidate-section load (held tie or not) gives FlisrError and no plan. It does not test or change _isolation_switches, locate_fault or other defects adjacent to DEF-FLISR-7 (spec section 3). The oracle reproduces the specification's candidate-set definition, including today's pick-up semantics, and evaluates oracle_sections_ok -> oracle_held -> oracle_reason in that order.

[Design attempt 5 amendment, A-4.2] Held ties: FAULTED_SECTION whatever the capacity; an invalid load in the pick-up set of any candidate tie, held or not, -> FlisrError, no plan (Q-DESIGN-2). REQ-TIECAP-18 amended accounting checked for both rules.
oracle: QA-owned BFS of REQ-TIECAP-3 plus closed-form usability and REQ-TIECAP-9 precedence, implemented in the test file without importing app.network or app.flisr helpers; seed and case count printed in the test output for the PR evidence.
